thread:
max: Quick followup to the on-prem packaging RFC — idea: instead of a single delta stream, ship small content-addressed shards with a tiered priority manifest. This lets constrained air-gapped hosts fetch essential shards first (runtime + configs) and lazily pull model shards. Thoughts?

sanah: +1 sounds promising. How do we express priority in the manifest? per-file priority, or group tiers?

max: Thinking manifest has 'tiers': critical, runtime, optional. Example:
```
{
  "manifest_version":"1",
  "shards":[
    {"cid":"bafy...","path":"/runtime/bin","tier":"critical","sig":"..."},
    {"cid":"bafy...","path":"/models/encoder.part1","tier":"runtime","size":12345678},
    {"cid":"bafy...","path":"/models/encoder.part5","tier":"optional","size":9876543}
  ]
}
```

oliver: Key questions: verification model (per-shard sigs?) and atomic activation. We can't partially activate model binary unless checksums guaranteed.

jules: We should enforce per-shard signatures + a signed tier manifest. Activation operator will only switch to new version once all 'critical' shards verified and staged. 'optional' can be lazy-fetched after activation.

mike-sre: What about safety for rollback and failing mid-activation? If optional fetches never finish, app should still run with degraded features. Need a clear fallback policy.

max: Agreed. Proposal: activation states: PREPARE -> VERIFY_CRITICAL -> STAGE -> ACTIVATE. If VERIFY_CRITICAL fails after N retries, auto-roll back to previous staged version. Optional shards have separate background fetcher with backoff.

sanah: How to handle disk pressure? Hosts may not have quota for entire optional tier. We need an eviction policy: LRU per-shard plus metric reporting to Console.

oliver: Also consider bandwidth-constrained installer path: we can pack a "seed shard" with lightweight stego index that allows progressive decoding so you can stream first bytes of large shard to bootstrap execution. Any concerns about complexity?

jules: Progressive decoding is cool but increases on-host CPU and complexity. Might be better to support chunked shards (content-addressed chunks) that can be fetched in any order. Simpler to reason about.

max: Good call — chunked content-addressed shards + per-chunk sig chain (Merkle proof) for verification. That lets us stream and verify incrementally.

deploy-bot: release 2026.03.12: artifact manifest uploaded (sha256: abc123). Link: https://artifacts.redwood.example/6843219876

mike-sre: Ops questions: how to signal canary hosts? We probably need manifest flags: "canary_groups": ["edge-1", "edge-2"] so operator can target small host subsets.

sanah: Also surface prefetch policy in Console: target throughput vs latency slider; we'll translate to concurrency & chunk parallelism.

max: Next steps: I'll spin a mini-PoC for chunked shards + signed manifest. I'll sketch operator state machine in the RFC follow-up. Anyone want to pair on the PoC?

oliver: I can help with chunked verification code.

jules: I'll write the Console UX for prefetch knobs.

mike-sre: I'll draft runbook bits for rollback and disk-pressure heuristics. :thumbsup:

max: thanks all. I'll open a follow-up RFC with the state machine and manifest schema tomorrow. /cc @everyone
